candidates.title: [Bug]: Cast to `T & readonly` over a list/mapping constructor panics with "bad type cast"
[Bug]: toBalString of negative infinity produces invalid expression `float:-Infinity`
candidates.body:
### Description

`value:toBalString` of a float -Infinity (on its own or inside a structure) produces `float:-Infinity`. That is not a valid Ballerina expression: nutcracker itself rejects `float x = float:-Infinity;` with `SYNTAX_ERROR: missing identifier`. The expected form is `-float:Infinity`.

### Steps to Reproduce

```ballerina
import ballerina/io;

public function main() {
    float x = -float:Infinity;
    io:println(x.toBalString()); // @output -float:Infinity
    io:println([x].toBalString()); // @output [-float:Infinity]
}
```

Run with `go run ./cli/cmd run <file>.bal`

**Expected:**
```
-float:Infinity
[-float:Infinity]
```

**Actual:**
```
float:-Infinity
[float:-Infinity]
```

**Spec reasoning:**

§5.9.5 (ToString, expression style): "when v belongs to anydata and does not have cycles, it will produce a string that is a valid Ballerina expression, such that evaluating that string will result in a value v' for which DeepEquals(v, v') is true". `float:-Infinity` does not parse, while `-float:Infinity` evaluates to -∞.

Note: the corpus currently codifies the wrong output at `corpus/bal/subset10/10-value/tobalstring-v.bal:71` (`// @output float:-Infinity`), with a matching line in `corpus/integration/subset10/10-value/tobalstring-v.txtar`. Both need updating along with the fix.

### Affected Version(s)

nutcracker (ballerina-nutcracker/ballerina) `main` @ 47f4de21aa0d12a7f050599bb97d19daf1692f7a

### OS, DB, other environment details and versions

Linux, Go 1.27.1

### Related area

Runtime

candidates.title: [Bug]: float:round(x, fractionDigits) rounds the decimal string instead of the exact binary value
candidates.body:
### Description

`float:round(x, fractionDigits)` gives the wrong result when the float's exact binary value is just below a decimal midpoint. For example, `2.675` is stored as 2.67499999999999982…, so rounding to 2 digits should give 2.67, but nutcracker gives 2.68. It looks like the shortest decimal string is being rounded half-even, rather than the exact value. Some cases come out right, e.g. `(1.005).round(2)` gives `1.0`.

### Steps to Reproduce

```ballerina
import ballerina/io;

public function main() {
    // 2.675 is stored as 2.67499999999999982236431605997495353221893310546875
    io:println((2.675).round(2)); // @output 2.67
    // 0.15 is stored as 0.1499999999999999944488848768742172978818416595458984375
    io:println((0.15).round(1)); // @output 0.1
    // 0.35 is stored as 0.34999999999999997779553950749686919152736663818359375
    io:println((0.35).round(1)); // @output 0.3
}
```

Run with `go run ./cli/cmd run <file>.bal`

**Expected:**
```
2.67
0.1
0.3
```

**Actual:**
```
2.68
0.2
0.4
```

**Spec reasoning:**

lang.float `round`: "Returns the float value that is an integral multiple of 10 raised to the power of `-fractionDigits` and closest to `x`. If there are two such values, choose the one whose final digit is even". Each `x` here is strictly below the midpoint (see the comments in the reproducer), so this is not a tie and the closest multiple is the lower one. The existing corpus round tests (`subset9/09-langlibs/float1-v.bal`) have no near-tie cases.

### Affected Version(s)

nutcracker (ballerina-nutcracker/ballerina) `main` @ 47f4de21aa0d12a7f050599bb97d19daf1692f7a

### OS, DB, other environment details and versions

Linux, Go 1.27.1

### Related area

Runtime

### Related issue(s) (optional)

#1029 (a different `float:round(fractionDigits)` precision bug)

[Bug]: XML template drops whitespace text that follows a processing instruction
candidates.body:
### Description

In an XML template expression, character data right after a processing instruction loses its leading whitespace. A whitespace-only run disappears completely, which also changes the number of items in the sequence. Whitespace after a comment is kept, and `xml:fromString("<?p q?>  x")` keeps it, so only the template path is affected.

### Steps to Reproduce

```ballerina
import ballerina/io;

public function main() {
    xml x = xml `<?p q?>   x`;
    io:println("[", x, "]"); // @output [<?p q?>   x]
    xml y = xml `<r><?p q?> <c/></r>`;
    io:println(y); // @output <r><?p q?> <c/></r>
    io:println((y/*).length()); // @output 3
}
```

Run with `go run ./cli/cmd run <file>.bal`

**Expected:**
```
[<?p q?>   x]
<r><?p q?> <c/></r>
3
```

**Actual:**
```
[<?p q?>x]
<r><?p q?><c/></r>
2
```

**Spec reasoning:**

§6.6.2 xml-template-expr: "The result of the previous step is parsed as XML content. More precisely, it is parsed using the production content in the W3C XML Recommendation." In XML 1.0, `content ::= CharData? ((element | Reference | CDSect | PI | Comment) CharData?)*`, and the PI production ends at `?>`. So the whitespace after it is CharData and must become (part of) a text item (§5.3: "A text singleton corresponds to one or more character information items"). No corpus test codifies the current behaviour.

### Affected Version(s)

nutcracker (ballerina-nutcracker/ballerina) `main` @ 47f4de21aa0d12a7f050599bb97d19daf1692f7a

### OS, DB, other environment details and versions

Linux, Go 1.27.1

### Related area

Parser

notes:
Stopped at the 5-confirmed-candidate cap (about 25 minutes in). The spec was fetched from ballerina.io/spec/lang/master. Note: the hunters said the saved copy appears to be 2022R4 and has no group-by/collect text.

GitHub issue search: `gh api search/issues` returned 403 (the session is bound to repo endpoints), so dedup paged through all 799 issues via `repos/ballerina-nutcracker/ballerina/issues?state=all` and filtered them locally.

Dropped as duplicates of open issues (all still reproduce on main):
- is-check ignores the shape of immutable lists/maps (#1044)
- casting away an error is not rejected (#1332)
- a cast's static type is not intersected with the operand type (#1130); `int y = <readonly>x` is a variant not yet listed there
- decimal division drops the IEEE preferred exponent (#1347)
- rest param list is read-only (#1424)
- anon-function default reading a captured local crashes with a Go interface conversion (#1151)
- named args evaluated in parameter order (#1166)
- readonly record field value is not read-only (#1134)
- filler value ignores field defaults (#1050)
- unary -/~ keep the narrow operand type (#1046)
- no singleton typing for * / % shift bitwise (#1262)
- compound assignment evaluates the lvexpr before the RHS (#1217)

Unprocessed leads (found after or alongside the cap; not deduped through the full pipeline and not spec-validated unless noted). Worth a future run:
1. `xml:strip` removes whitespace-only text before removing comments/PIs, so `(xml ` ` + xml `<!--c-->` + xml `b`).strip()` gives `b` instead of ` b`. Spec-validated and no issue found, but jBallerina parity is uncertain. Repro: /tmp/claude-0/hunt-xml/f4.bal.
2. A query `let` clause does not use its declared type as the initializer's expected type: `let float f = 1` and `let float[] fs = [1,2]` are rejected. Not validated.
3. A field from an included object type (`*T`) is never checked for initialization, so it is nil at runtime: `<nil> + int64` crash.
4. Calling `self.init()` from a method re-runs the field initializers; `c.init()` on a non-self receiver is not rejected.
5. `obj.toString()` / `toBalString()` on an object without that method gives "method not found" instead of falling back to the lang.value function.
6. A method default `int d = self.x` crashes at runtime (Go interface conversion); `self.x + 1` gives `fatal[INTERNAL_ERROR]: expression type not resolved`.
7. Any XML template with an interpolation produces a read-only value (spec 6.6.2 says only inside a const-expr). Corpus `10-xml-navigation/lang-xml-errors-v.bal:207-230` codifies the current behaviour, so it needs a maintainer decision.
8. The `xml:` prefix in an XML template attribute (`xml:lang`) is rejected as an undefined namespace prefix.
9. After `group by`, aggregated variables are accepted in any expression (e.g. a mapping field value, an order-by key). The 2024R1 spec rule was not verified.
10. A computed key followed by a literal field with the same name (`{[k]: 1, a: 2}`) silently keeps 2; per 6.7.2 the result should be `{"a":1}`.

Scratch reproducers are in /tmp/claude-0/hunt-* (ephemeral container).
